name: Bell 412
summary: Four-blade development of the Bell 212 used in the US mostly by law enforcement, firefighting, EMS and offshore operators.

wings: Four-blade main rotor on a short, compact hub
engines: Twin-Pac engine with two exhausts side by side on the roof
Wide rear engine cowling like the Bell 212
fuselage: Boxy Huey-style cabin with large sliding doors
Skids (wheels on some), often with floats or a hoist
Plain rounded nose, sometimes with a weather radar bulge
tail: Two-blade tail rotor on the fin

tellTales: Classic boxy utility cabin on skids but with four main rotor blades
Two exhausts side by side and only a two-blade tail rotor
Civil paint, often police, fire or EMS

confusedWith.howToTell: The 412 has a four-blade main rotor; the UH-1/205/212 has two blades.
The UH-1Y has a four-blade tail rotor, FLIR nose and Marine gray paint; the 412 keeps a two-blade tail rotor.
The AW139 has five blades, a sleek nose and retractable wheels; the 412 has four blades on a boxy Huey cabin with skids.
The Bell 214ST is larger, longer and bulkier than the 412; the 412 has a more compact body.
The Bell 222/430 have a smoother body and a long swept nose; the 412 is a boxy utility machine with a blunt nose.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
